answer: The cobbler keeps a last for every customer, and the register holds the measure of each foot the shop has ever fitted. A glacier pair made on another last fails the register: at the harbor of the instep the leather must follow the customer's own measure, and a strange pair pinches at the first step. Forging a pair means buying lasts, hiring a cobbler and paying 5,200, while the delta entry in the register is read at every fitting, so shoes whose last was never entered are refused.
